simple.meaning: אוּפָז (ʼÛwphâz) is a Hebrew word meaning “Uphaz , a famous gold region.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אוּפָז (H210) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Jeremiah 10:9, with occurrences in Jeremiah, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אוּפָז (H210) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אוּפָז (H210) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אוּפָז (ʼÛwphâz) / H210 is traced through Jeremiah 10:9, Daniel 10:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H210. Uphaz אוּפָז ( proper name, of a location unknown & dubious) whence came gold, מֵא ׳זָהָב Jer 10:9 ; א ׳ֶכּתֶם Dan 10:5 ; so Thes 1Kin 10:18 מוּפָז זָהָב ( מוּפָז = ׳מֵא ); but ᵐ5 δόκιμος , & 2Chr 9:17 טָהוֺר , whence MV Klo make מוּפָז Hoph`al Participle from פזז q. v. Klo reads אוֺפִיר (q. v.) for אוּפָז Jer 10:9 ; Dan 10:5 , in view of אוֺפִיר כֶּתֶם Isa 13:12 . **Corrupt, see Siegf ThLz, Nov. 7, 1883, 530 ; he explained ׳מֵא Jer 10:9 as error for מוּפָז 1Kin 10:18 , and ׳א Dan 10:5 as borrowed from Jer 10:9 ; in 10:9 Gie reads מֵאוֺפִיר , Du either this or מוּפָז (see פזז ); read מֵאוֺפִיר perhaps also Dan 10:5 (Dr).

occurrences.englishText: There is silver beaten into plates, which is brought from Tarshish,
